newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RAND WATER HIKES WATER PRICES, MORE IN PIPELINE.
newsitem.headline: RAND WATER HIKES WATER PRICES, MORE IN PIPELINE.

text.p: Rand Water announced on Thursday that the price of water supplied to local authorities and mines would rise by eight percent from April 1 and a further 22 percent from October this year.
The move follows a government announcement earlier this week that water tariffs would be increased to cover higher operating and catchment management costs.
Rand Water supplies bulk water to local authorities which, in turn, set their own tariffs.

Chief executive Vincent Bath said that while the latest increase was slightly below inflation, the high capital cost of the Lesotho Highlands Water Project (LHWP) would mean water price increases over the next year would be above inflation.
He said an increase of 31.92 cents per kilolitre was planned for October. This would bring the cost of a kilolitre of water to 176.18 cents.
Schalk van der Merwe, general manager of scientific services, told Reuters the October increase would be specifically linked to a levy to finance South Africa's contribution to the LHWP scheme.
The LHWP is a $5 billion join venture by Lesotho and South Africa which aims to tap the landlocked mountain kingdom's abundant water resources for the benefit of both countries.
"Our geographical situation means that we have to draw our water from further and further afield, with consequent cost implications," Bath said.
"This means that the best way to stabilise the cost of water into the future would be to moderate consumption and achieve savings on costly new infrastructure," he added.
